picks.reasoning: Tennessee is the No. 8 team and comes in with momentum. It beat Kentucky 34-6 and ran for 240 yards behind DeSean Bishop, who has over 1,000 rushing yards. A&M is also missing key pieces, including two offensive linemen and several receivers, and WR Mario Craver is questionable. The risk is real: Tennessee has a growing injury list, including its sack leader Tyree Weathersby and two offensive linemen, and it is playing a road game at Kyle Field. A short spread on a game this tight could easily come down to a single field goal. The -114 price is from a pre-game BetMGM listing and may have moved.

picks.event: New York Rangers at Vancouver Canucks
picks.reasoning: The Rangers are the better team and the market has them at roughly 68%. That price looks a little too high. Dimers' model puts the Canucks at about 35.7% against the roughly 33% implied by the +203 price, and the Canucks get Filip Chytil back from injury and play at home. The Rangers are starting Joonas Korpisalo with Igor Shesterkin out for the season. This is a thin edge on a bad team (17 losses in 20 games, 31st in expected-goals share), so expect to lose this bet about two times in three. The odds are an approximate conversion of Novig's 33¢ price, so check your own book before betting.

picks.event: Washington Commanders at New York Giants
picks.reasoning: The Giants have a strong defense and are 6-2 against the spread. Jayden Daniels should face heavy pressure, and a Giants offense with an injury-limited J.J. McCarthy (hip) may lean on the run and shorten the game. The total sits at 41 to 41.5 depending on the book, so the price is fair and not a bargain. I like the Under over the spread because the Giants line has already moved from -1.5 to -2.5, which removes the value on that side. Football totals are volatile and McCarthy's status adds uncertainty, so this is a small edge at best.

This is essentially a pick'em between the top two teams in the East. Boston (8-2) is fully healthy with no injuries listed, and Tatum is averaging 27.1 points. Philadelphia is thin up front, with Bona and Barlow out and Embiid managing a foot issue, though he is expected to play. Tony's Picks has Boston about 3.3 points better, and Dimers shows a 4.5% edge on Boston to win, yet the market has the Celtics at roughly -105 to -121. The best available price of -105 at BetRivers is close to even money. Treat this as a small edge in a toss-up, not a lock, because Embiid's status and a road game in a hostile building both add risk.

picks.event: New Orleans Pelicans at Golden State Warriors
picks.reasoning: Golden State has won seven straight, but it is laying 9.5 points. That is a bigger number than the one it laid at home against Memphis, and the line has moved between -8.5 and -9.5 all day. The Warriors are thin: Butler, Moody, Porzingis and Richard are out, and Green and Podziemski have recently dealt with back issues. New Orleans has only Yves Missi listed as out. Double-digit NBA spreads are often too large, and the Pelicans can score with Murphy, Williamson and Murray. Counterpoints: New Orleans is on the second night of a back-to-back after playing at the Clippers on Sunday, it has a weak defense (about 121 points allowed per game), and Curry is scoring more than 35 a night over the last five games. I'm treating this as a small-edge play on the number, not a strong lean.

picks.event: Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears
picks.reasoning: Chicago is the better team at 6-2, but a 6.5-point spread is a lot for a Bears side that just played Monday night and lost starting left tackle Braxton Jones for the season. Tampa Bay is mostly healthy: WR Emeka Egbuka and LT Tristan Wirfs both look set to play. Their one absence is OLB Yaya Diaby. The Bucs also have a strong run game and are on a two-game win streak. Getting more than a touchdown covers the key numbers of 6 and 7 in a game with a 47.5 total. Some books list Bears -6 or -5.5, so shop for the best number. The risk is that Chicago's explosive offense wins comfortably, and the Bears are 7-3 in their last 10 home games.

picks.event: Miami Hurricanes at Notre Dame Fighting Irish
picks.reasoning: The No. 1 and undefeated Hurricanes have Darian Mensah, one of the country's most efficient QBs. The line has moved from Notre Dame -5.5 or -3.5 at the open to about -7 after WR Malachi Toney's ankle injury. That looks like a slight overreaction for a team that still has plenty of passing talent. Notre Dame is also missing LB Drayk Bowen and CB DJ McKinney. Seven is a key number, so you're buying the hook-ish side of a game that is likely to be close and high-scoring. Miami is 1-9 all-time at South Bend, Toney is out, and a Notre Dame win by exactly 7 would push, so the edge is small and the uncertainty is real.

The 76ers are 8-1 and have the league's 2nd-ranked defense (105.3 defensive rating). The Cavaliers are 4-4 and have several rotation players banged up. Jarrett Allen, Tyrese Proctor and Peyton Watson are questionable, and Jaylon Tyson is out. I'm taking the short -1.5 spread at -114 because the number is small and the price is better than the -132 moneyline. Spreads vary by book (-1.5 to -2.5). The 76ers' offense is mediocre (21st), and the Cavaliers' offense is strong (6th) at home. This is a thin edge, not a lock, and Allen's status could move the line.

Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are both on injured reserve. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano starts his first game on a sore ankle, and he managed only 91 passing yards in relief last week. Baltimore will probably lean on its run game and defense, and Jacksonville has no reason to push the pace as a big favorite, so a low-scoring game is likely. The total has already fallen from 42.5 to 39.5, so some of the value is gone. A Jaguars blowout or a few defensive or special-teams touchdowns could still push it over, so this is a small-edge play. The price is -108 at BetRivers and about -102 elsewhere.

This is a matchup of the East's two best records, and Detroit's defense is a strength. The Pistons won the first meeting 106-93 on Oct. 25, which finished well under this total. Duren (hamstring) and Isaiah Joe (hip) are out for Detroit, and Barlow and Hukporti are out for Philly. Those absences thin out depth on both sides more than they add scoring. Other books have this total as high as 219.5, so -106 at 217.5 is the best price I found. The edge is small, and one hot shooting night or an Embiid return could push it over, so treat this as a modest lean.

picks.event: Edmonton Oilers at New Jersey Devils
picks.reasoning: One source lists the Devils at -158 and the Oilers at +130, which implies Edmonton wins about 43.5% of the time. Dimers' model puts the Oilers at about 46.6%, so the price looks slightly generous. Edmonton has won three of its four games as an underdog this season. The risks are real. Goalie Frederik Andersen is out with a knee injury, Zach Hyman is on injured reserve, and New Jersey is strong at home (6-2). Other books show the Oilers anywhere from about +102 to +130, so only take this if you can get plus money of +120 or better, and treat it as a small edge rather than a strong play.

Seattle is a 3-point home favorite, and that is the most common margin in the NFL, so the +3 is worth a lot. The Bears' offense has looked strong since Caleb Williams came back from his hamstring injury. He has thrown for 300+ yards in back-to-back games with no interceptions. Seattle is also missing starting LT Charles Cross and WR Rashid Shaheed, and its replacement left tackle is shaky against a Bears pass rush that is back to full strength. The risks are real. Seattle's defense is elite and the game is in a tough road environment. Chicago is also without RB Kyle Monangai, so this is a small edge on a close game, not a confident pick.
picks.start_time: 8:15 PM ET (7:15 PM CT, Monday Night Football)

picks.reasoning: Lamar Jackson returns from a three-game ankle absence with no injury designation. He has had three full practices, though he says the ankle is still sore. The Ravens' record and recent results reflect games played without him, so the market may not fully price in his return. Buffalo is 5-1 and Josh Allen is the MVP front-runner, but the Bills have several players listed as questionable, including OT Spencer Brown, TE Dalton Kincaid and WR DJ Moore. Getting a field goal of cushion with a healthy Jackson is a small edge. A one-score game is likely, but Buffalo could still win by exactly 3 or more. Lines also vary by book, with +3.5 available at some.

This is a matchup of two 6-1 ranked Big 12 teams. Texas Tech's offense has been shaky: quarterback Will Hammond has been turnover-prone, and Tech has one of the least explosive passing attacks in the country. Arizona's defense allows about 4.7 yards per play, which is among the best in the nation. The line has drifted from Texas Tech -4.5 to -3.5, and the +3.5 sits right on the key number of 3. Arizona is short several receivers, and the price is only the BetMGM quote of 1.93 decimal, which converts to roughly -108. Taking the points gives a cushion in what looks like a low-scoring game, but this is a small edge and a one-score game could go either way.

Two computer models project about 219 total points, roughly 10 below the posted 228.5. Only one of the Knicks' five games and one of the 76ers' five games have gone over this number, and the average total in each team's games has been lower than 228.5. The sources disagree on who is favored and by how much, so the side is too murky to bet. The total is the more consistent edge. The -110 price is a typical estimate, not a quoted line, so check the actual number before betting. Early-season samples are small and a hot shooting night can sink any under.

The line is close to a pick'em, and the Cavaliers are 3-1 and on a three-game winning streak. The Hawks are 2-3 and just lost 129-117 to Miami. Injury reports show no major Cavs rotation players out (only Tomlin out and Diop day-to-day), and the Hawks are missing Gueye and Veesaar. Both teams are on the second night of a back-to-back, so rest doesn't favor either side. One model I found rates Cleveland about 55% to win, which against roughly even odds gives a small edge. That's a thin edge in a coin-flip game early in the season, and odds vary by book (some show the Cavs at -108), so shop for the best price.

The Cavaliers are a healthy, heavy favorite, but 9.5 points looks like too many for a game in October. One computer model projects a Cleveland win by about 8, and another puts the Wizards' cover chance near 55% with roughly a 6% edge. Washington is missing Jamir Watkins, Tristan Vukcevic and Justin Champagnie, and AJ Dybantsa is questionable with an ankle injury, so check the injury report before tip-off. This is a small-edge value play on the spread, and Cleveland could easily win by double digits.

picks.event: Detroit Pistons at New York Knicks
picks.reasoning: Detroit is 3-0 and has a strong defense and a strong Cade Cunningham. The Knicks are 0-3 and have struggled to score, and they are still priced as home favorites of about 3.5 to 4 points. The Pistons are short-handed. Jalen Duren is out, and Ausar Thompson and Isaiah Joe are questionable. Those absences are probably already in the line, and a 3-0 start is a small sample. Treat this as a modest-value spread play rather than a strong edge. Check the injury news before tip-off, because a Thompson absence would weaken the case.

Houston closed as only a 1.5-point road favorite when these teams met on Saturday and won 121-114. Monday's line is -5 to -5.5, which looks like a big jump for home court plus VanVleet returning. The market has barely moved, and about 71% of spread tickets are on Houston, which suggests the number leans toward the public side. Atlanta is healthy apart from two minor absences, and the Rockets are thin up front with Adams out and Smart questionable. Early-season samples are small and Houston could still win comfortably, so this is a small edge. Odds are approximate (-110 at -5.0 to -5.5), so check the final number before betting.

Denver has the league's second-best defense by opponent rating and is 3-0 on the road. Arizona is 2-4, gives up more touchdowns than any other team, and has lost RB James Conner to injured reserve and traded away WR Marvin Harrison Jr. FPI gives Denver about a 69% win chance and the Squawka model about 79%. Both put the margin at roughly 5 to 9 points, which is above the 4.5 spread. The risk is Denver's offense. Bo Nix has struggled for weeks and the Broncos have been outscored on the season. Several expert picks also lean Arizona, so a close game or an upset is a real possibility.
picks.start_time: 4:05 PM ET (2:05 PM MT / 1:05 PM local in Glendale, AZ)

picks.reasoning: Houston played the Spurs on Oct. 23, so this is the second night of a back-to-back. Reed Sheppard (knee) is out, and Fred VanVleet may also be rested. Atlanta is home and rested, and is 2-0 with a strong defense. Dimers' model puts the Hawks near 58% against a market price of about 50% to 55%. Early-season NBA samples are tiny, and Houston has Sengun and Durant, so the game is close to a toss-up. Odds also vary by book, with Hawks ML listed from -120 to +100, so shop for the best price.

Indiana won 19 games last season and Dallas won 26, yet the Pacers are 6.5-point favorites, and the line has moved from -5.5 to -6.5 since open. Early-season NBA spreads this large tend to overrate small samples, such as Indiana's 1-0 start. Indiana is also missing T.J. McConnell and Johnny Furphy, with Nesmith and Sheppard questionable. Dallas has Cooper Flagg, though Kyrie Irving, Dereck Lively and Santi Aldama are all day-to-day, which could hurt. Dallas lost its opener by 18, and this is a thin-edge play at roughly a coin-flip price, with a real chance the Pacers cover.

picks.event: New England Patriots at Chicago Bears
picks.reasoning: New England is missing both starting guards (Vera-Tucker and Brown), starting CB Carlton Davis and two reserve corners. Right tackle Morgan Moses is also questionable. That is a lot of attrition for a road team on a short week. Chicago is mostly healthy at home, with RG Jonah Jackson cleared to play. Dimers' model gives the Bears about a 62% win probability and a cover edge, while the market has them as only a field-goal favorite. The risks are that a 3-point spread can land exactly on 3, and that New England is 4-2 and has been playing well, so this is a thin edge and not a lock.

This is a near pick'em on opening night, and the market has barely moved. The Heat are only -1.5 at home, and 62% of spread tickets are on Minnesota. Both teams are close to fully healthy. Minnesota's only absence is DiVincenzo, and Goldin is questionable for Miami. Minnesota starts Edwards and LaMelo Ball, so its perimeter shooting should help against a Heat team built around Giannis and Bam inside. Taking the points costs about the same as the moneyline and covers a one-point loss. Opening-night rotations, new rosters and no regular-season sample make this very uncertain, and it is a small edge at best.

The Knicks are the defending champs and open at home, and last season's net rating gap of about 6.5 points favors them by more than this spread. Embiid and James aren't on Philly's first injury report, but Simons is questionable and the new-look Sixers have little chemistry. Josh Hart's ankle is a minor concern, and Mike Brown doesn't expect it to keep him out. Opening-night variance is high and the line has already moved from -3.5 to about -4.5, so this is a small edge. I'd skip it if the number goes past -5.

Jayden Daniels is back at quarterback and 49ers pass rusher Nick Bosa is sitting. That makes a 7.5-point spread look a bit high for a Washington team that tied the Giants 27-27 in overtime last week. About 78% of spread bets are on San Francisco, yet the line hasn't moved off -7.5 and the price has shifted slightly toward Washington. The 49ers are unbeaten and cover well (4-1 ATS), and Washington is winless on the road. At -115 the bet needs to win about 53.5% of the time, so the edge is small and this is a modest-value play, not a strong one.

Atlanta is at home and getting points against a Bears team that is thin on defense. Chicago is missing T.J. Edwards and Montez Sweat. Caleb Williams is returning from a torn hamstring after three missed games, so rust is possible. Michael Penix Jr. is expected back from his rib injury, and Atlanta has averaged 34.3 points in his three starts, with Bijan Robinson leading the NFL in rushing yards. Sharp money has reportedly backed Atlanta at +1.5 to +3, and +1.5 is a thin edge. Penix's status and Williams's fitness are both uncertain, and the -110 price is approximate because books differ slightly.

picks.event: Tampa Bay Rays at Cleveland Guardians (ALCS Game 4)
picks.reasoning: Tampa Bay is a 98-win team facing a must-win spot. It has a real starter in Nick Martinez (15-6, 3.10 ERA, rested eight days). Cleveland is expected to use Shawn Armstrong as an opener and then go to a bullpen game. The market has this as nearly a pick'em, so the home-team premium looks small, and the Rays' starting-pitching edge and 5-1 regular-season record against Cleveland aren't fully priced in. Cleveland's bullpen has been excellent and the Guardians lead the series 2-1, so this is a thin edge on a high-variance single game, not a strong lean.

Seattle has the league's top defense in yards allowed per game, and it pressures quarterbacks at a high rate. That matches up well against Bo Nix, who has struggled this season: he has been under 190 passing yards in three of five games and has an 80.8 passer rating. Seattle has also won straight-up after every loss since the start of last season, and Denver is 1-4 against the spread on Thursdays under Sean Payton. The risks are real. -2.5 is a thin margin, Seattle's offensive line has allowed nine sacks and Darnold is under heavy pressure, and Denver's blitz has produced seven takeaways. A low-scoring game could turn on one turnover, so treat this as a small lean.
